newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Credit Bank president to resign - paper.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Credit Bank president to resign - paper.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd president Hiroshi Kubota will resign to take responsibility for a deterioration in the bank's financial status, the Japanese mass-circulation daily Yomiuri Shimbun reported on Monday.
The paper said Kubota will announce his resignation at the same time as the bank unveils a restructuring plan later this week.

Kubota, a former director-general of the National Tax Administration Agency, joined the bank in 1993 after serving as president of the government-funded Hokkaido-Tohoku Development Corp. He became the bank's president in June the same year.
Kubota is likely to remain the bank's chairman, a post he assumed last year, because the bank needs his leadership to successfully execute its rehabilitation plan, the paper said.
A bank spokesman said the newspaper report was purely speculation and that nothing of the sort had yet been decided.
